newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Caterpillar Belgium, unions in compromise deal.
newsitem.headline: Caterpillar Belgium, unions in compromise deal.

text.p: Management and striking workers at the Belgian unit of U.S. earth-moving equipment maker Caterpillar have reached agreement on a compromise deal, both sides said on Wednesday.
The accord, reached after more than half a day of last-ditch talks, brings to an end a dispute which began on May 16 and caused production to stop for a total 50 days.

The deal, which runs from January 1, 1997, to December 31, 1999, involves management revoking a decision to sack 227, mainly young, blue-collar workers and cutting investment for 1997 by 20 percent to achieve necessary economies.
In return, unions accept early retirement at the age of 52 years and new, reduced pay, contracts for staff hired from January 1, 1997. Existing contracts would not be changed.

The conflict was over a five-year 1.8-billion-franc cost cutting plan to boost competitiveness, which included savings of 300 million francs on wages. Under the new deal the savings on wages will be only 250 million francs.
The deal came after three attempts at arbitration failed. The plant currently employs some 2,500 blue-collar workers and 1,000 white-collar staff.
